messages.subject: Error: Too few degrees of freedom
messages.subject_clean: Error: Too few degrees of freedom
messages.body_plain:
Dear dr. Chalmers,
My colleagues have found some problem with degrees of freedom. I understand why the model is not identified with too many parameters and small number of possible different response patterns.

On the other hand, the model fails also in multi-group analysis and I suppose in such case, the possible response patterns should be multiplied by the number of groups. See an example in attachment, which was provided by colleagues. With 5 binary items and four groups, 40 parameters are freely estimated with 2**5-1=31 d.f. - and thus the model is not estimated with this warning:

## Error: Too few degrees of freedom. There are only 31 degrees of freedom but 40 parameters were freely estimated.

I am quite sure the real number of d.f. is 31*4 = 124. Am I right? Is there any possibility to fix the problem?
Thanks,
Hynek

messages.subject: Understanding simdata behavior
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil, all,

I was trying to understand how mirt creating a pattern response given a probability (P). If I understand correctly, P is calculated using the provided a,d, guess, upper, theta parameters and passed to respSample function.

https://rdrr.io/cran/mirt/src/R/simdata.R

for <https://rdrr.io/r/base/Control.html>(i in <https://rdrr.io/r/base/Control.html> 1L:nitems) data <https://rdrr.io/r/utils/data.html>[ <https://rdrr.io/r/base/Extract.html>,i] <- respSample <https://rdrr.io/cran/mirt/src/R/utils.R>(prob.list[ <https://rdrr.io/r/base/Extract.html>[i]])

respSample seems to be in c and I cannot find its implementation.

https://rdrr.io/cran/mirt/src/R/utils.R#sym-respSample
respSample <- function(P) .CallC'respSample", P)

What does it do exactly, for items of type unidimensional '2PL', for example? What it uses as a reference threshold to determine if it returns a '0' or a '1'

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Hugo

messages.body_plain:
The C++ function is here: https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/blob/368a99bb98503e92524b307621bd9f1fc82559e6/src/Misc.cpp#L378

This is just an optimized wrapper to something analogous to sample.int <http://sample.int>(), but is intended to be a little faster since the whole probability matrix is passed to C++ at once to avoid multiple bridge translations between R and C objects. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Constraining items that have different number of observed categories
messages.subject_clean: Constraining items that have different number of observed categories
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

I have a question about equal constraints to item parameters in Multidimensional GRM (but the multidimensionality is not essential).

Now, I'm analyzing data that is collected under the 2 times repeated measurement design. The same items are used in 2 measurement points and the questionnaire consists of 7-point scale.

Assuming the ordinal scale and no parameters drift, I tried using MGRM with equal constraints between time1 and 2, and latent traits differ by the point.

In some items, however, the number of observed categories was different between times.

i.e,) In item 3 at time 1 , 1,2,3,4,5,**7** are observed, but, in item 3 at time2, 1,2,3,4,5,**6** are observed.

I tried to constrain category boundary parameters in item 3 between measurement points, `mirt` returned error below

```
CONSTRAIN = ... indexed a parameter that was not relevant for item 3
```

How to constraints under this condition?
Or, any other ideas?

messages.subject: Fixed calibration - how to make mirt calibrate with MWU-MEM method
messages.subject_clean: Fixed calibration - how to make mirt calibrate with MWU-MEM method
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am using the following code to implement fixed calibration with MIRT, but only recently I came to realize that, depending on the estimation method used, the obtained parameters can be extremely biased - see Kim attached. How can I set MIRT to use the method  Multiple Prior Weights Updating and Multiple EM Cycles (MWU-MEM) as described in the attached paper? Can I?

parameters <- mirt( data=mt_ef5_scored_filtered[,-c(13)],
                    model=models,
                    itemtype='3PL',
                    technical=list(NCYCLES=1000),
                    pars="values")

for(i in c(2:9,11,12,14:30)){
  parameters[ ((parameters$item == paste0("Q",i)) & (parameters$name == "a1")),]$value <- pars[i,"a"]
  parameters[ ((parameters$item == paste0("Q",i)) & (parameters$name == "d")),]$value <- pars[i,"d"]
  parameters[ ((parameters$item == paste0("Q",i)) & (parameters$name == "g")),]$value <- pars[i,"c"]

  parameters[ ((parameters$item == paste0("Q",i)) & (parameters$name == "a1")),]$est <- FALSE
  parameters[ ((parameters$item == paste0("Q",i)) & (parameters$name == "d")),]$est <- FALSE
  parameters[ ((parameters$item == paste0("Q",i)) & (parameters$name == "g")),]$est <- FALSE
}

mod_mt <- mirt( data=mt_ef5_scored_filtered[,-c(13)],
                model=models,
                itemtype='3PL',
                technical=list(NCYCLES=10000),
                pars = parameters)

coef(mod_mt,simplify=TRUE,IRTpars = TRUE)
profic_mt_raw = fscores(mod_mt) #estimativas das proficiÃªncias individuais

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Hugo

messages.subject: Re: Constraining items that have different number of observed categories
messages.subject_clean: Constraining items that have different number of observed categories
messages.body_plain:
It's possible to "trick" mirt into ghosting in categories by using the technical = list(customK) input, where you specify how many levels are in the category theoretically rather than based on the observations. This gets a little tricky in that including the additional parameters that should not be present runs the risk of non-identification, in which case these parameters *must* be constrained to be equal to something else in order for them to be properly identified. Inspecting the starting values is important when using this approach, and the downside is that the data are still translating into a suitable dummy coded form internally, so matching parameters across items will require some care. Though in general, for models such as these such an expansion will potentially be less meaningful since the constraints don't really matter (there's no valid observations to constrain for each category in some cases), and it probably is more justifiable just to freely estimate the categories that do not match across time (e.g., don't constrain time 1 cat 7's parameters to time 2 cat 6's since they represent different observed responses, but constrain everything else since they do represent the same changes). HTH.

Phil
